findings.detail: raised by queue_count at connections.permit (mission fix_permits_in_batches)
findings.fix: Region.queue_at (and use_tool's queue_count) read Network.queue_of for any step, but a wait or material step has no queue: guard it as Region.measures does (count 0), and add a test that counts the queue at connections.permit.
findings.id: error:Invalid access to property or key '<RefCounted>' on a base object of type 'Dictionary[SimStep, Array]'. (network.gd:203 in Network.queue_of)
findings.title: Engine error: Invalid access to property or key '<RefCounted>' on a base object of type 'Dictionary[SimStep, Array]'. (network.gd:203 in Network.queue_of)

findings.detail: open problems no active mission covers at the end of the run; they hold one of Region.MAX_OPEN (4) slots, so missions get refused with problem_unavailable
findings.fix: When a mission fails or completes without solving its problem (deadline missed, an investigate goal), put the problem back to sleep (Region.deactivate) or keep a mission open for it. A failed save_henks_knowledge can never be accepted again (status failed), so its problem stays open for good, against 'the problem can still be solved another way'.
findings.title: Problems stay open (and hurting) with no mission to solve them

findings.detail: Region.MAX_OPEN problems are open, mostly problems without a mission (see the orphan finding)
findings.fix: Count only problems with an active mission towards MAX_OPEN, or hide such missions from the board with the reason.
findings.title: Missions on the board cannot be accepted (problem_unavailable)

findings.detail: Against a no-fix twin (same network, same random sequence), the expert's best fix moves the problem's own KPI by under 1 % for 5 of 19 problems and makes it worse for 8 (the team hours the experiment takes), mean over seeds. The before/after columns meanwhile move 18 % on average from the stream's own trend. Flat: incomplete_application/lead_time, installer_not_ready/lead_time, revision_backlog/throughput, digging_damage/lead_time, grid_study_queue/throughput. Worse: custom_design/throughput -7 %, not_at_home/first_time_right -5 %, inverters_tripping/first_time_right -1 %, status_callers/on_time -4 %, done_but_not_closed/lead_time -5 %, transformer_wait/wip_age -5 %, unused_capacity/lead_time -1 %, silo_kpis/first_time_right -3 %.
findings.fix: Lagging KPIs (lead time, first time right, on time) measure orders that started long before the fix, and the Check passes on fit alone, so the table carries no lesson. Show the after-window against a no-fix twin (as fade_forecast does), ask for a leading-indicator prediction in the A3, or measure lagging KPIs only on orders that entered after the fix.
findings.title: The Check's 14 days cannot show the fix in the problem's own KPI

findings.detail: average/11: 15 of 46 completed missions were re-runs of a faded fix; the campaign took 252 days (campaign_done) against the expert's 165
findings.fix: A reopened main mission takes the only main slot for another 14+ days, so new missions wait. Let a reopened mission come back as a side mission (or a short 're-standardise' task without a new Check), and make decay_days longer than the Check so one lapse is not a full redo.
findings.title: Treadmill: players who do not always standardise spend most of the campaign redoing faded fixes

findings.detail: careless ends at € -462.613 after 1097 days, still falling about € 13.840 a month; 4 bad periods
findings.fix: CLAUDE.md: recovery must always be possible. Open problems (and worn fixes) keep costing and the bad period cuts capacity, while rewards come only from solved problems. Add a floor (e.g. the board grants a recovery budget, or costs stop at a debt limit), or let a bad period lower costs (no overtime) instead of only capacity.
findings.title: Debt spiral: the budget keeps falling and the bad period never ends

findings.detail: cm standard_van_stock, predicted on_time -7.1 %, problem KPI on_time -7.1 %, capacity +49.9 %, eff 0.72, lesson cause_right; against the no-fix twin on_time +3.5 %
findings.fix: Before/after compares two different 14-day windows, so the stream's own trend (and noise) lands on the player's fix. The expert's counterfactual (same network, same random sequence, no fix) shows the fix improved the KPI. Compare the after-window with a no-fix twin, as GameSession.fade_forecast already does, and show 'zonder jouw maatregel' as the reference column.
findings.title: The Check table shows the problem's KPI worse although the fix helped

findings.detail: cm request_permits_daily, predicted lead_time +13.2 %, problem KPI lead_time +13.2 %, capacity -3.9 %, eff 0.10, lesson mismatch
findings.fix: The mismatch/too-early verdict contradicts the table (trend or noise). Show the no-fix reference, or word it 'de cijfers bewegen, maar niet door jouw maatregel'.
findings.title: Check fails while a KPI improved more than 5 %

findings.detail: cm standard_van_stock, predicted wip_age +100.0 %, problem KPI on_time -12.8 %, capacity +26.0 %, eff 0.72, lesson cause_right
findings.fix: Show the problem's KPI as the headline row; word a pass with a worse headline as 'de maatregel werkt, maar het effect is nog niet zichtbaar'.
findings.title: Check passes while the problem's own KPI got worse (prediction named another KPI)

findings.detail: cm standard_designs, predicted throughput -29.2 %, problem KPI throughput -29.2 %, capacity +26.2 %, eff 0.90, lesson cause_right; against the no-fix twin throughput -9.8 %
findings.fix: The pass rule is the countermeasure's fit (eff >= 0.5), not the numbers; a leading indicator (capacity, throughput, WIP age) is supposed to move inside the Check. Judge the pass on the measured change against a no-fix twin, or have the panel say 'geslaagd, maar je voorspelde KPI is nog niet bewogen'.
findings.title: Check passes while the predicted leading KPI got worse

findings.detail: 46 missions after 1097 days
findings.fix: See the slowest missions; shorten Checks or let the player run missions in parallel.
findings.title: Campaign not finished within the horizon

findings.detail: 3 seeds: 20000 XP, budget € 231.770, 165 days each, although the Check numbers differ per seed
findings.fix: Pass, score and rewards come from fit, maturity and planned capacity (Capacity.analyse), never from the measured flow. Let the impact dimension (and a bonus) use the measured change against a no-fix twin so that what the player sees in the numbers is what they are rewarded for.
findings.title: The simulation never changes an outcome: the expert's result is identical on every seed

findings.detail: cm delegated_approval, predicted throughput +86.5 %, problem KPI throughput +86.5 %, capacity +86.7 %, eff 0.55, lesson cause_wrong
findings.fix: By design the fit decides the pass and the lesson says cause_wrong, so a lucky countermeasure passes. Lower eff when the cause is wrong (e.g. x0.6), or make the root-cause dimension of the score cost more.
findings.title: A wrong root cause still passes the Check

findings.detail: cm standard_van_stock, predicted on_time -7.1 %, problem KPI on_time -7.1 %, capacity +49.9 %, eff 0.72, lesson cause_right; against the no-fix twin on_time +3.5 %
findings.fix: The panel's LAGGING_NOTE explains lag in general, but not when the predicted KPI moved the wrong way. Name it in the verdict ('je voorspelde KPI is een volgindicator: kijk naar de stuurindicatoren') or let the A3 ask for a leading indicator as the prediction.
findings.title: Check passes while the predicted lagging KPI got worse

findings.detail: cm daytime_outage_crew, predicted first_time_right +51.3 %, problem KPI first_time_right +51.3 %, capacity -2.4 %, eff 0.90, lesson cause_right; against the no-fix twin first_time_right +10.4 %
findings.fix: Check that the countermeasure's effects touch the constraint's touch time or availability; otherwise the 'bottleneck first' lesson reads false.
findings.title: A fix at the constraint passes but stream capacity does not rise

findings.detail: cm early_transformer_order, predicted wip_age -0.2 %, problem KPI wip_age -0.2 %, capacity -0.0 %, eff 0.90, lesson cause_right; against the no-fix twin wip_age -10.3 %
findings.fix: Make the countermeasure's effect large enough to move its KPI inside 14 days, or let the panel name the indicator that did move.
findings.title: Check passes with no visible change in the predicted or the problem KPI

findings.detail: the impact dimension rewards stream capacity only; a wait (permit, delivery, close-out) has no team, so the expert's right fix scores impact 1-2 and gets the 'not the bottleneck' note
findings.fix: Score impact on the problem's KPI against the no-fix twin (lead time for a wait), not on capacity alone.
findings.title: Fixing a wait step can never score on impact

findings.detail: master black on day 107 of a 165-day campaign; belts on days yellow 22, green 24, black 50, master_black 107
findings.fix: Total campaign XP (~20000 for the expert) is far above Progression's master black (12000). Raise the belt thresholds, scale XP down, or tie the later belts to maturity and the KPI review instead of XP.
findings.title: Belts run out early: the top belt comes long before the campaign ends

findings.detail: save_henks_knowledge failed on day 115 with its problem check_ready; the problem stays open with no mission
findings.fix: Count the deadline as met once the A3 is submitted (the countermeasure is in place), or warn when the Check would end after the deadline.
findings.title: A deadline runs out while the player's experiment is already running

findings.detail: 40 distinct lines over 450 expert asks; 11 lines reach 5+ missions, e.g. "Wat wil je bereiken? Hoe ziet het eruit als het hier goed loopt?" in 14 missions. Insights: 84 of 450 asks.
findings.fix: The question index restarts at 0 for every mission, so each mission opens with the same line. Rotate by mission (offset by a hash of the id or by missions completed) and add a few mission-specific questions next to the insights.
findings.title: The coach repeats the same questions across missions

findings.detail: cm close_out_at_completion, predicted lead_time +8.7 %, problem KPI lead_time +8.7 %, capacity +0.0 %, eff 0.90, lesson cause_right; against the no-fix twin lead_time -4.9 %
findings.fix: A wait step has no team, so at_constraint is always false and the panel says 'het werk wacht nog op een ander team'. Skip the warning (or word it for waits) when the problem's step is a wait.
findings.title: 'Not the bottleneck' warning on a problem at a wait step

findings.detail: reopenings per run (the expert standardises every fix and audits on every 'slipping' event)
findings.fix: Working as designed for players who do not standardise; check the reopened mission tells why it is back.
findings.title: Fixes fade and missions reopen

findings.detail: failed on day 115 (taken on: true), closes ["skills_matrix_buddy"]
findings.fix: Working as designed (a missed deadline closes a door); see the orphan finding for what happens to its problem.
findings.title: Deadline missed: save_henks_knowledge
